info.name: searxng-integration-test
info.description:
Direct requests to the local SearXNG instance (container/docker-compose.yml), the same way a metasearch client (Firecrawl, Hermes, a browser bookmark) calls it. SearXNG has no authentication: whatever address SEARXNG_HOST publishes (container/.env) is an open search proxy for that network.

container/core-config/settings.yml must keep search.formats [html, json] - without json, clients get 200 responses with no results array.

Firecrawl's own view of this instance (/v2/search mappers) is tested in the firecrawl project's collection, folder "SearXNG (local search provider)".

{{searxngUrl}} is a collection variable so these run without an environment; point it at the published host.

The collection carries one pre-request guard: a request whose host variable does not resolve to a real URL is skipped with a console warning naming the variable, which is what a shared-link copy (no collection variable, no environment selected) produces.

request.description: The call Firecrawl makes for a web search: GET /search with format=json. mappers.web turns content into description and drops everything else, so these extra fields (template, engines, parsed_url) never reach a Firecrawl caller. categories=general is what Firecrawl sends when SEARXNG_CATEGORIES is empty.

request.description: categories=news is the news half of the mapping: mappers.news renames content to snippet and publishedDate to date. Firecrawl sends SEARXNG_NEWS_CATEGORIES here (default news) and, per the comment in search/v2/searxng.ts, deliberately sends no engines pin - a pin like "yahoo,mwmbl" would leave the news category with no engine to run.

const same = images.filter(r => r && r.url && r.img_src && r.url === r.img_src);
console.log(images.length + ' image result(s), ' + same.length + ' with url === img_src');

request.description: categories=images. mappers.images keeps url as the page the image was found on and renames img_src to imageUrl - the pair Firecrawl returns as {url, title, imageUrl}. Engines differ here in how they fill those, which is why only the presence of both fields is asserted.

exec: pm.expect(body.results, 'safesearch=2 emptied a benign query; check the enabled engines honour safesearch').to.have.length.above(0);

request.description: safesearch=2 is strict, and it is the only thing /v2/search safe:true adds to the SearXNG request (search/v2/searxng.ts sends it only when safe is set, otherwise the instance default applies). How much each engine honours it varies, so this asserts the parameter is accepted and the query still answers rather than pinning a result count. The Jev filter that runs on top of safe:true is a separate stage, covered by the Search Safe Filter folder.
